**Compare total cost at equivalent useful quality and service requirements.** An API bill depends on input/output token volumes and their prices. A custom deployment adds fixed engineering and training amortization plus variable serving cost, idle capacity, redundancy, and maintenance. [1](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)

In a simplified model, let API cost per comparable unit be p, custom variable cost c, and custom fixed monthly cost F. Equality gives $V^*=F/(p-c)$ when p exceeds c. For illustrative values F=10,000 and p-c=0.002, break-even is five million units per month. These are example inputs, not current market prices.

**QPS alone is insufficient.** Convert requests to tokens, account for length distribution, peak headroom, and target p99. Include evaluation, failed experiments, retraining, and operational staffing.

Privacy or contractual constraints may independently rule out an option. Establish an API or pretrained-model baseline before assuming months of custom training are justified. A routed small-model tier or distillation may offer an intermediate path. The decision should use measured domain quality and real lifecycle costs, not parameter count or a single GPU-hour estimate.

**Technical details and references.**

Compare options at matched domain quality and SLOs. Let API monthly cost be $V_{in}p_{in}+V_{out}p_{out}$, with prices expressed per token after unit conversion. Let custom monthly cost be fixed operations/training amortization $F$ plus workload-dependent serving $Vc$. If API cost per comparable unit is $p>c$, break-even is $V^*=F/(p-c)$; otherwise volume alone gives no break-even. [1](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)

Convert QPS into monthly tokens using input/output lengths, utilization, peak headroom, and redundancy. Include engineering time, retraining, evaluation, failed experiments, storage, and idle GPU capacity. Privacy constraints and contractual terms can rule out options independently of price; measure p99 end-to-end latency and domain accuracy on held-out tasks. Consider an API baseline, a small-model routing tier, or distillation before assuming three months of custom training is justified.
